summary: In addition to its literary value, Karel Čapek’s 1920 drama Rossum’s Universal Robots (R.U.R.) is famous for popularizing the term “robot” worldwide. The phrase, which comes from the Czech word “robot,” which means hardship or forced labor, perfectly captures the main idea of the play: artificial beings made to serve humanity who eventually rebel.
